reading.text:
Reading of the clause "the solution depends on eps: a tuple solving at two strengths has
vanishing correction, and in the specialisation no tuple solves at two strengths" (Example 5.5,
last two paragraphs, 05-examples.tex ~350-470).

Model (Example 5.5 on Example 5.1(i)): n = m = d = 1, G = 1, nu sigma-finite on countably
generated E (nu != 0 in sec. 5 for Ex 5.4/5.5), xi_0 in L2(F_0), sigma_c in R, h_c in L2(nu),
beta_1, beta_2 > 0, h_x in L2(nu), strength eps >= 0. Coefficients
  b = -beta_1 y, sigma = sigma_c - beta_1 z,
  h = h_c + h_x x - beta_1 u - eps A_{mu^U}(u),  f = beta_2 x + <h_x, u>_{L2(nu)},  g(x,rho) = x,
mu^U the U-marginal of the measure argument (for h: of mu_s^- = Law(Theta_s^-), whose U-marginal
is Law(U_s)); A_lambda(u) = int_{L2(nu)} gradV(u - v) lambda(dv) (Bochner integral in L2(nu)),
gradV(w) = w / sqrt(1 + ||w||^2). "Solves the system at strength eps" = is a solution in S of
(1.1) with these coefficients (the Solution notion), on the standing basis.

Specialisation: E = {-1,+1} x (0,1], nu(dvarsigma,dq) = c_varsigma q^{-1-rho} dq, 0 < rho < 2,
c_{+-1} = (2-rho)/2; beta_1 = 1, beta_2 = 1/2, sigma_c = 1, xi_0 = 0, h_c(varsigma,q) =
varsigma q, h_x(varsigma,q) = q; T > 0 arbitrary.

Paper's claim (last paragraph): for every eps > 0 the solution Theta^eps has
E int_0^T ||eps A_{Law U^eps_t}(U^eps_t)||^2 dt > 0; "The solution therefore depends on eps: if
one tuple solved the system at two strengths, subtracting the forward equations and the
compensated-Poisson isometry would force the crowding correction to vanish dt(x)dP-a.e."

A faithful formal statement has two conjuncts:
 (a) [vanishing correction] For the dealer system (general data as above, or at least the
     specialisation; the argument uses only the two forward equations, so the general form is a
     broader statement whose instance is the specialisation), for all strengths eps != eps'
     and every tuple Theta in S that solves the system at eps and at eps':
     A_{Law(U_t)}(U_t) = 0 in L2(nu) for dt(x)dP-a.e. (t,omega) in [0,T] x Omega
     (equivalently E int_0^T ||A_{Law U_t}(U_t)||^2 dt = 0).
 (b) [dependence on eps] In the specialisation, for every T > 0, every rho in (0,2), every
     standing basis carrying this nu, and all eps != eps' (in [0, inf); a statement over all
     reals is broader and still true by the paper's argument), there is no tuple Theta in S
     solving the system at both eps and eps'.
Quantifier order: model data / basis first, then the two strengths, then the tuple. Narrower if:
rho fixed to a single value, T fixed, a particular basis only, eps' restricted (e.g. only eps' =
0 or only eps, eps' > 0), or the tuple class restricted below S. Mismatched if it claims only
"Theta^eps != Theta^0" while naming it the two-strength statement, or if the coefficients differ
(e.g. missing h_x x / <h_x,u> terms, A evaluated against Law(Theta) instead of the U-marginal,
wrong sign of eps). Hypotheses: (a) needs a tuple solving at two strengths; that it is possibly
vacuous in the specialisation is exactly (b) -- the general (a) is a statement whose hypotheses
can be met in the h_x = 0 case (the inert tuple of the "interaction is active" paragraph solves at
every eps), which is a good witness.

comparison.text:
Comparison: Dissertation.PaperSpec.A.ex_dealer_depends (PaperSpec/A/Sec5DealerActive.lean:218-252)
against my reading.

Coefficients ex55Coeffs ν β₁ β₂ σc hc hx ε (Sec5Dealer.lean:44): b = -β₁ y, σ = σc - β₁ z,
h = hc + x hx - β₁ u - ε A_{μ^U}(u), f = β₂ x + <hx, u>, g(x,ρ) = x; μ^U = margU μ = image of μ
under the projection on the jump channel (Law/TupleMarginal.lean:82); A = ex55Crowd
(Sec5.lean:631): A_Λ(u) = ∫ (1+‖u-v‖²)^{-1/2} (u - v) Λ(dv), Bochner in L2(ν). Exactly the
paper's coefficients (sign of ε, exposure terms, U-marginal). In a Solution, h is evaluated at
(Θ⁻_s, μ⁻_s), whose U-marginal is Law(U_s): as in the paper.

Conjunct (a): for every standing basis with d = 1 (LevyDriver P 1 ν, ν σ-finite, E countably
generated, 𝒢₀ independent), T > 0, β₁, β₂ > 0, σc, hc, hx in L2(ν), ε, ε' >= 0, ε ≠ ε', any ξ₀,
any tuple: Solution at ε and Solution at ε' (same ξ₀) ⇒ for a.e. s in [0,T], a.s.,
A_{Law(U_s)}(U_s) = 0, with Law(U_s) = margU of Law(Θ⁻_s) and U_s the L2(ν) class of
U_s(ω,·). This is my (a): vanishing correction dt⊗dP-a.e. (iterated a.e., the natural reading),
for the general data of the example. It is broader than the printed context in two harmless ways:
ξ₀ is arbitrary (Example 5.1(i) takes ξ₀ ∈ L2(F_0)) and ν = 0 is not excluded (sec. 5 takes
ν ≠ 0 for Examples 5.4-5.5); and it is stated for the example's general data, not only the
specialisation in whose paragraph the sentence stands (the argument is general).

Conjunct (b): for every ϱ in (0,2), every standing basis with d = 1 and ν = ex55Marks ϱ =
dealerMarks (c ≡ (2-ϱ)/2) ϱ, i.e. density c_ς q^{-1-ϱ} against counting x Lebesgue on
E = Bool x (0,1] (Examples/Dealer/Marks.lean:119), every T > 0, hc, hx the L2(ν) classes of
ς q (true ↦ +1) and q, and all ε ≠ ε' in [0,∞): no tuple is a Solution at both ε and ε' with
β₁ = 1, β₂ = 1/2, σc = 1, ξ₀ = 0. This is my (b) exactly: all ϱ, all T, every basis, all pairs
of distinct nonnegative strengths (pairs with 0 included).

Quantifier order: data/basis, then strengths, then tuple. Solution is the reviewed S-solution
notion. Hypotheses can be met: the witness ex_dealer_spec_hypotheses (Acceptance/A/
Sec5DealerActive.lean:306) exhibits ϱ = 1, the classes hc, hx, and a probability space with a
LevyDriver for ex55Marks 1 and 𝒢₀ = ⊥ independent (LevyDriver.exists), so (b) is not about an
empty setting. For (a), the antecedent (a tuple solving at two strengths) is satisfiable in the
inert case h_x = 0 (stated in ex_dealer_inert: the tuple solves at every ε'), so (a) is not
vacuous either.

Verdict: broader (conjunct (a) drops ξ₀ ∈ L2(F_0) and ν ≠ 0 and is stated for all dealer data);
the printed claim is the instance with those hypotheses, or the specialisation; (b) is exact.

verdict.detail: Conjunct (a) (vanishing correction for a tuple solving at two strengths) is stated for all data of Example 5.5: any σ-finite ν, including ν = 0, any initial datum ξ₀ rather than ξ₀ ∈ L2(Ω,F_0), and any β₁, β₂ > 0, σ_c, h_c, h_x. The printed sentence stands in the specialisation paragraph, but its argument is general. The printed claim is the instance with ξ₀ ∈ L2(F_0) and ν ≠ 0, in particular the specialisation (β₁ = 1, β₂ = 1/2, σ_c = 1, ξ₀ = 0, ν = ex55Marks ϱ, h_c = ς q, h_x = q). Conjunct (b) is the printed specialisation exactly: for every ϱ ∈ (0,2), every T > 0, every basis and every pair ε ≠ ε' ≥ 0, no tuple solves at both strengths.

author_review.disagreements: The recorded review says "faithful". It points to a report filed under another unit (ex_dealer_active), so it may not be a review of this proposition. I record "broader". Conjunct (a), vanishing correction for a tuple solving at two strengths, is stated for all data of Example 5.5: any σ-finite ν, including ν = 0, and any initial datum ξ₀ instead of ξ₀ ∈ L2(F_0). The printed sentence stands in the specialisation paragraph. The printed claim is therefore an instance of (a), not (a) itself. Conjunct (b) matches the specialisation exactly. This is a disagreement of label within the "matches" group: nothing in the proposition is wrong or narrower.
